**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disambiguate the unmount button query**

In this test's initial controlled state, both the always-rendered button above and the button inside the open popup have the accessible name `Unmount root`, so `screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Unmount root' })` throws with multiple matches before the remount assertion runs. Rename one button or scope the query to the intended container so this regression test can pass.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Notify detached triggers after resetting handle state**

When the handle-backed Root remounts in a subtree that does not also rerender the detached triggers (for example a persistent header trigger with a route-owned Root), this direct state replacement resets `open`/`activeTriggerId` without notifying the existing trigger subscribers. Those triggers can keep stale `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, data-state, and interaction props from the pre-unmount open dialog until some unrelated store update happens, even though the remounted Root is closed. Avoid the render-time notification if needed, but schedule a post-commit notification or otherwise resubscribe the detached triggers after the reset.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve trigger registrations when detaching the store**

When a route-owned `<Dialog.Root>` unmounts while detached header triggers using the same handle stay mounted, this cleanup drops the attached store without moving its `triggerElements` back into `pendingTriggerRegistrations`. Those triggers only re-render on the store-pointer change; their stable ref callback is not invoked again, so the next root attaches with an empty trigger map. After that remount, `handle.open('trigger')` cannot find the still-mounted trigger, so it opens unassociated and loses trigger-owned payload/ARIA/focus behavior until the user physically clicks the trigger.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Drop stale registrations when reattaching handles**

When a live `<Dialog.Root>` switches from handle A to handle B while detached triggers for handle A stay mounted, this attaches the same root-owned store to handle B without removing handle A's trigger registrations. Those trigger refs are stable and only re-render on the store-pointer notification, so they never unregister from `newStore`; handle B can then count or resolve handle A's triggers, causing `handleB.open(oldId)` or implicit trigger ownership to use the wrong trigger/payload/focus relationship.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep detached fallback triggers inert**

When a detached trigger remains mounted after its route-owned `<Dialog.Root>` unmounts, `useDialogHandleStore(handle)` returns the handle's fallback store here, so the trigger is still fully wired to `useClick`. Clicking that trigger while no root is attached mutates the fallback store to `open`, leaving the button with `aria-expanded="true"`/open data state but no popup or `aria-controls` target until another click or remount. Either make the fallback store ignore open changes or gate trigger interaction/ARIA on an attached root store.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore the previous root when the latest overlap detaches**

When two roots share a handle during a transition and the newer root unmounts before the older one (for example, a canceled route transition), this cleanup drops `attachedStore` to `null` even though another root using the same handle is still mounted. The older root's effect does not rerun, so detached triggers and `handle.open()`/`close()` remain inert until some later attach, leaving a mounted root uncontrollable by its handle. Track the remaining attached stores and restore the previous one instead of clearing the handle unconditionally.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Migrate fallback triggers before activating a root**

When a detached trigger is already mounted in the fallback store and a root mounts, this switches `attachedStore` to the new root store before any of those fallback registrations have been copied or the trigger has rerendered to re-register. If `handle.open('trigger')` is called from a layout effect in the same mount commit after the root attaches, the open path only consults the new store’s empty trigger map and opens unassociated, dropping the trigger payload/ARIA relationship and focus return. This is a same-commit gap in the final code because registration migration is deferred to a later subscriber/ref rerender rather than being made available synchronously here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Attach the handle before child layout effects can open**

When a component rendered inside this `<Dialog.Root>` calls `handle.open()` or `openWithPayload()` from a mount `useLayoutEffect`/`useIsoLayoutEffect`, React runs descendant layout effects before this parent hook's layout effect, so `attachedStore` is still `null` and the call is ignored even though the root is mounting. This regresses effect-driven openings that the previous handle-owned store allowed; attach the store before descendant layout effects can run, or otherwise queue same-commit opens until the attach completes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The descendant-mount-useLayoutEffect open path is an accepted consequence of the root-owned-store model. Developers who hit it already get the dev warning, and the workarounds are straightforward — open from a passive useEffect, an event handler, the defaultOpen prop, or the dialog context (any descendant of Dialog.Root has access to it).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid claiming unassociated opens during migration**

When a detached trigger re-registers because its handle store pointer changed, this also reapplies trigger data. If the root was opened imperatively without a trigger before the detached triggers have migrated (for example `handle.open(null)` or `openWithPayload()` from a layout effect in the same commit that the root attaches), `activeTriggerId` is still `null` and `open` is true, so `applyTriggerData` claims the first migrating trigger and can overwrite an `openWithPayload()` payload with the trigger's payload. That makes an explicitly unassociated imperative open become trigger-associated only during root attach/remount timing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
